text: A station can be accessible. Its network may not be. This is UNLOCK, the accessibility impact graph.

Every morning, lift outages arrive as free text. Paste one in. UNLOCK finds the exact lift in its Relate graph, from the station, and the platforms fifty and fifty-one that this lift serves. No guessing.
One click simulates the outage. The published data is not touched, but platforms fifty and fifty-one are cut off. Twenty-one confirmed step-free connections are lost.
Why? This is the actual path in the graph: platform forty, lift A.S.C. eight, the underpass, lift A.S.C. three, platform fifty. Two lifts in series, each with its published status and source file.
Now rank every repair across the region. Fixing this lift restores twenty-one connections, ahead of two lifts that are really out of service today.
With the repair, the network returns exactly to its published state, and an independent Cypher query agrees with the engine.
A vague report is never guessed: UNLOCK asks which lift. And it shows the lifts you can't afford to lose: one hundred and ninety-one single points of failure today.
The same graph is an M.C.P. server, so an A.I. agent answers with real numbers and evidence, instead of inventing them.
UNLOCK doesn't just show you what's broken. It shows you what fixing it makes possible.
